unit.title: Agents for teachers’ work, checked and approved

lesson.title: A task in steps
lesson.subtitle: Hand an agent a job in steps, and plan the checks too

video.title: A task in steps
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: The road; The weather; A reminder.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: On Friday my class visits a farm in Dala. I want an agent to check the road and the weather, and remind me to tell the parents. Will it do them in the right order?

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: handing an agent a task in steps.

scenes.visual: A list: First, find something; Then act on it; Plan, then tool after tool.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A job is a chain of steps
scenes.narration: Most school jobs take more than one step: find something, then act on it. An agent plans the steps, then calls one tool after another.

scenes.visual: A list: Steps, in order; A tool for each step; Which result feeds which step; Darsi Tiny: one line.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A plan is the list of steps an agent will take, in order, with a tool for each. A good plan also says which step needs which result. Darsi Tiny writes its plan in one line.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s Darsi Tiny with a two-step goal: six B’s first lesson tomorrow, and a reminder at seven thirty. First the timetable, which answers P E. Then the reminder, written from that result: six B, P E.

scenes.visual: A list: Route: Kafi to Dala, 70 km; Weather in Dala: partly cloudy, 32°C; One answer from both results.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The trip has the same shape. The route tool says Kafi to Dala is seventy kilometres. Then the weather tool checks Dala: partly cloudy, a high of thirty-two.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! On Saturday there’s no school, so the timetable answers: no school. What does Darsi Tiny do next?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: It still sets the reminder, six B, six B, for Saturday. It never checked the timetable’s answer before using it. Big models can make the same slip. So the check after each step must be built in, by the app or by you.

scenes.visual: A list: Plan the steps and their tools; Check each result before the next; Stop for a yes before any action.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So plan the checks too. After a step that finds something, look at the result. Before a step that acts, like a reminder or a message, the app should stop for your yes.

scenes.visual: A list: Absences, then a draft note; A word, then library books; First lesson, then a reminder.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Many teacher jobs fit this shape. Find who was absent this week, then draft a note for each family. Look up a word, then find library books about it. Check tomorrow’s first lesson, then set a reminder.

scenes.visual: A list: Pick a goal, guess its tools; Compare with Darsi Tiny’s plan; Chips: where each word came from; Try Saturday.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, pick a goal and guess its tools, in order. Then compare your plan with Darsi Tiny’s. Coloured chips show where each word of a call came from. And try Saturday.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. In the reminder six B, P E, where did the words P E come from?

scenes.visual: Summary points: A chain of steps, each with a tool; One result feeds the next step; Check after each step.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A chain of steps, each with a tool · One result feeds the next step · Check after each step
scenes.narration: From the timetable’s result. Remember: a job is a chain of steps, each with a tool. One step’s result can feed the next. And a failed step can still lead to an action, so check after each step.

scenes.visual: A list: Plan a trip as tool steps; A card per step: tool, needs, gives; Mark where a person checks; What if a step fails?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: plan a class trip as tool steps. Groups write each step on a card: the tool, what it needs, and what it gives back. Then they mark where a person checks, and what happens if a step fails.

checkpoints.prompt: On Saturday the timetable answers “no school”. What does Darsi Tiny do next?

options.text: It stops and tells you there’s no school
It asks which day you meant

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it never checks the timetable’s answer, so it carries on and sets a useless reminder. The check after each step has to be built in.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — Darsi Tiny carries on: it sets the reminder “6B: 6B” for Saturday, because it never checks a result before using it.

checkpoints.prompt: In the reminder “6B: PE”, where did “PE” come from?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the request only said 6B. PE came back from the timetable tool, and the second call used it.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — you only said 6B. PE came from the timetable’s result, and the reminder used it.
